how: A request recruits helpers to convert a flag, and a later proposal supplies coordinates and a shared placing time.
A participant judges the attempt outnumbered and recommends defending another flag instead.
A one-line answer joins the timed heart takeover without requesting anything in return.
A participant answers the initial request by reporting a tile placed.
The timed proposal receives an explicit bare join, supporting the local call-and-answer relation without establishing a general conversational obligation.
The initial caller proposes a flag conversion that another participant answers with a placement report.
Starting and calling can occupy the same request rather than appearing as successive observable stages.
Participants propose a national flag and an additional picture at another location.
A tile-placement report makes individual building work visible in the thread.
A participant reports that only the red portion of an additional picture has been made.
An explicit coordinate answer makes the image findable for a participant asking where it is.
Coordinate sharing supports location without requiring a template or demonstrating that design disagreement has been settled.
The request for help receives a direct report of placing a tile, supporting reported participation after the call.
Visible proposals and joins do not establish whether decisions about leadership or work division occurred elsewhere.
Reports of individual tile placement and replacement do not reveal whether automation or spare accounts also contributed.
Participants replace changed tiles and explicitly agree to watch the picture to keep it unchanged.
A report of replacing an overwritten tile receives explicit agreement that keeping the achieved picture unchanged is the task.
Existing-picture upkeep can coexist with another participant extending the effort at a second location.
Repair is evidenced, but neither automation nor a shortage making it necessary is established.
A changed tile is reported without investigating the placer's identity, affiliation, or motive.
An outnumbered participant proposes helping another flag, without evidence that help was delivered or reciprocated.
A proposal to help another flag can arise from an initially outnumbered attempt before maintaining an achieved picture.
The speaker explicitly uses being outnumbered as the reason to recommend helping another flag instead.
Exploratory switching of proposed targets can precede any documented erasure or overrun of the room's work.
A capacity judgment precedes that speaker's new target, but the stated selection reasons do not establish capacity as the cause of moving.
Justifying conversion because another copy remains does not evidence restraint or refusal to cover another work.
Takeover proposals do not establish negotiation, consent, a border agreement, or a truce.
Recommending help for another flag does not establish a coalition.
A report of another building location does not establish a host's rule or permission to build there.
The suggestion to help another flag does not show anyone carrying a proposal between rooms.
Conversion proposals supply no agreement whose authority could be disputed, so this record cannot test the tentative representation process.
Without an evidenced agreement or representation dispute, the tentative agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism cannot be tested.
Watching and repairing the picture do not establish subsequent border negotiations.
Conversion justified by spare copies does not establish restraint produced by a negotiated border.
The recommendation to help another flag contains no preceding border agreement or bargain.
Repair reports do not establish that upkeep led to coalition membership.
Participants reuse national officials and civic honours as a mock reward for canvas achievement.
Nationally named targets are selected through existing colours and spare copies without an evidenced prior tie naming the rival.
Practical target-selection reasons do not establish a quarrel carried in from before the canvas.
A mock civic award within canvas celebration does not establish that the host subreddit was framed as an April Fools prank.
The help request and its answers do not establish moderator containment or changed rules for canvas talk.
A posted call does not establish the flood or subsequent moderation required by the proposed mechanism.
A success title receives congratulations, followed by a mock civic award and an appreciative reply.
Reported achievement and celebration are present, but the edited acquisition claim does not establish the arrow's precise timing or causal mechanism.
Announcing completion can precede continuing repair rather than require the work to remain finished without upkeep.
Success can be celebrated while the picture's identity remains unsettled for a later viewer.
The citable success title does not establish what its associated image records or whether participants intended archival preservation.
Celebration and mock rewards do not establish a decision to continue the effort beyond the canvas.
The final question concerns the live picture before closure and cannot test disputes over versions retained after placement ends.
Celebration is evidenced without an established transition to archival recording.
The success announcement and later identification question do not establish archiving that motivates continued organisation.
Participants call for converting existing flags and hearts into their desired mark.
Calling for conversion can be the original means of building the room's mark rather than a later diversion of recruited hands.
Participants choose conversion targets requiring few changed pixels and justify covering a work because its makers have another copy.
A capacity-based redirection is insufficient evidence of restraint when the same speaker subsequently proposes converting another flag.
The conversion proposals do not establish a subsequent negotiation or invocation of a truce.
The success title does not identify a defeated rival or establish an exchange of contest talk with another room.
Conversion and celebration are evidenced without a transition into talk conducted against a rival room.
Make interpreting an achieved picture explicit in the process account because a later viewer questions its identity after success has been celebrated.
